tool_arguments.query: AWS segment revenue and operating income Q2 2026 Amazon earnings

events.content: AWS segment revenue and operating income Q2 2026 Amazon earnings

Amazon’s latest reported quarter is Q2 2026, released July 30, 2026. [[1]]

| AWS metric | Q2 2026 | YoY comparison |
|---|---:|---:|
| Segment revenue | **$42.2 billion** | **+37%** |
| Segment operating income | **$16.6 billion** | $10.2 billion in Q2 2025 |
| Operating margin | **39.4%** | — |
| Annualized revenue run rate | **$169 billion** | — |

AWS revenue was $42.232 billion, up 37% year over year, while AWS operating income was $16.621 billion versus $10.160 billion a year earlier; the implied/reported segment operating margin was 39.4%. [[1]] [[2]]

**AI contribution:** Amazon did not disclose a separate quarterly dollar revenue or operating-profit contribution from AI within AWS. [[1]] However, management said AWS’s AI business exceeded a **$25 billion annual revenue run rate** and was growing at a **triple-digit year-over-year percentage rate**. [[1]] Amazon also said its chips business—which includes its AI-related infrastructure offerings—exceeded a separate **$25 billion annual revenue run rate**, likewise with triple-digit growth. [[1]] 

At the consolidated level, Amazon reported Q2 operating income of **$27.5 billion**, up from $19.2 billion in Q2 2025, meaning AWS generated roughly 60% of company operating income in the quarter. [[1]] [[2]] Net income of $62.6 billion included **$53.4 billion of non-operating pre-tax other income**, primarily related to Amazon’s Anthropic investment, so that gain should not be interpreted as AWS operating performance or recurring AI operating profit. [[1]]

events.content: Microsoft Azure revenue Q3 fiscal 2025 YoY growth AI contribution

In Microsoft’s fiscal Q3 2026 (quarter ended March 31, 2026), Azure and other cloud-services revenue grew **40% year over year** (**39% in constant currency**). [[1]] 

AI services contributed approximately **12 percentage points** of that Azure growth, versus roughly **9 points** in the prior-year quarter; therefore, AI was about **30% of Azure’s reported 40% growth rate** (12 ÷ 40), with non-AI services accounting for the remaining ~28 points. [[2]] 

Separately, Microsoft said its total AI business reached a **$37 billion annual revenue run rate**, up **123% year over year**. [[3]]

tool_arguments.query: Amazon equity investment in Anthropic accounting valuation Q2 2026 10-Q

events.content: Amazon equity investment in Anthropic accounting valuation Q2 2026 10-Q

Amazon’s Anthropic investment is **not accounted for under the equity method**; Amazon records its Anthropic convertible debt as available-for-sale investments at fair value and adjusts its private-company equity investments—primarily including Anthropic—for observable price changes or impairment. [[1]] 

The accounting therefore differs by instrument: unrealized fair-value movements on the **convertible notes** initially run through accumulated other comprehensive income (AOCI), rather than operating profit or net income. [[2]] 

When portions of those notes convert into Anthropic nonvoting preferred shares, Amazon reclassifies the previously accumulated unrealized gain out of AOCI and into **“Other income (expense), net”** in the income statement. [[1]] 

The converted preferred shares are initially recognized at estimated fair value at conversion and subsequently adjusted for observable price changes or impairment, with those Level 3 adjustments recognized in **“Other income (expense), net.”** [[1]] 

Accordingly, the “valuation gain” is generally a **non-cash mark-up**, not proceeds from Amazon selling Anthropic shares; it reflects a new observable transaction or financing valuation for comparable Anthropic securities. [[1]] 

For FY2025, Amazon reported a **$15.2 billion net gain**, primarily attributable to upward valuation adjustments on Anthropic nonvoting preferred stock plus gains recycled from Anthropic convertible notes that converted during the year. [[3]] 

More specifically, FY2025 upward adjustments on private-company equity investments were **$7.7 billion**, primarily from Amazon’s Anthropic preferred stock, while the note-conversion-related AOCI reclassification was **$5.6 billion** through the first nine months of 2025. [[3]] [[1]] 

In Q3 2025 alone, Amazon said Anthropic-related investment gains added **$9.5 billion pre-tax** to non-operating income, comprising a $7.2 billion observable-price adjustment and a $2.3 billion AOCI reclassification associated with converted notes. [[4]] [[1]] 

The effect continued into 2026: in Q1, Amazon recognized approximately **$12.3 billion** of upward adjustment on Anthropic preferred stock and approximately **$4.5 billion** of gains from reclassifying convertible-note amounts into other income, contributing to **$16.8 billion of pre-tax Anthropic investment gains**. [[5]] [[6]]

tool_arguments.query: AWS AI contribution to revenue growth percentage point contribution Q2 2026

events.content: AWS AI contribution to revenue growth percentage point contribution Q2 2026

- **AWS growth:** AWS revenue was **$42.2 billion in Q2 2026**, up **36.7% year over year**—its fastest growth in 18 quarters—and Amazon said the business reached a **$169 billion annualized revenue run rate**. [[1]]

- **AI-revenue disclosure:** Amazon said AWS’s **AI business exceeded a $25 billion annual revenue run rate** and was growing at a **triple-digit year-over-year rate**; this equates to more than **$6.25 billion on a simple quarterly run-rate basis** and at least roughly **15% of AWS’s $169 billion annualized revenue**, although Amazon did not formally disclose quarterly AI revenue or its precise share of AWS growth. [[1]]

- **Management’s key comment on workload contribution:** Andy Jassy said AWS was seeing strong growth in both **AI** and **non-AI (“core”)** workloads, with each supporting the other rather than AI being an isolated revenue stream. [[2]]

- **Mechanism:** Management said AI adoption encourages customers to move to AWS and increases core-service consumption; moreover, post-training reinforcement learning and AI-agent tool use are largely CPU-intensive, benefiting AWS core compute as well as AI accelerators. [[3]]

- **Important caveat:** Therefore, it would be inaccurate to attribute all—or a defined portion—of the 36.7% AWS growth rate to AI: Amazon disclosed rapid AI revenue growth, but **did not quantify AI’s percentage-point contribution** to Q2 AWS growth. [[3, 1]]

function.arguments: {"query":"AWS AI contribution to revenue growth percentage point contribution Q2 2026"}

private_messages.content:
- **AWS growth:** AWS revenue was **$42.2 billion in Q2 2026**, up **36.7% year over year**—its fastest growth in 18 quarters—and Amazon said the business reached a **$169 billion annualized revenue run rate**. [[1]]

- **AI-revenue disclosure:** Amazon said AWS’s **AI business exceeded a $25 billion annual revenue run rate** and was growing at a **triple-digit year-over-year rate**; this equates to more than **$6.25 billion on a simple quarterly run-rate basis** and at least roughly **15% of AWS’s $169 billion annualized revenue**, although Amazon did not formally disclose quarterly AI revenue or its precise share of AWS growth. [[1]]

- **Management’s key comment on workload contribution:** Andy Jassy said AWS was seeing strong growth in both **AI** and **non-AI (“core”)** workloads, with each supporting the other rather than AI being an isolated revenue stream. [[2]]

- **Mechanism:** Management said AI adoption encourages customers to move to AWS and increases core-service consumption; moreover, post-training reinforcement learning and AI-agent tool use are largely CPU-intensive, benefiting AWS core compute as well as AI accelerators. [[3]]

- **Important caveat:** Therefore, it would be inaccurate to attribute all—or a defined portion—of the 36.7% AWS growth rate to AI: Amazon disclosed rapid AI revenue growth, but **did not quantify AI’s percentage-point contribution** to Q2 AWS growth. [[3, 1]]

Sources:
[S8.1] Amazon.com, Inc. - Amazon.com Announces Second Quarter Results — https://ir.aboutamazon.com/news-release/news-release-details/2026/Amazon-com-Announces-Second-Quarter-Results/

[S8.3] Amazon (AMZN) Q2 2026 Earnings Call Transcript — https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/07/amazon-amzn-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/

function.name: finish
function.arguments:
{"summary":"AWS segment (Q2 2026, released July 30 2026):
- Revenue: $42.2B, +36.7% YoY (fastest growth in 18 quarters), annualized run rate $169B.
- Operating income: $16.6B, up from $10.2B in Q2 2025; operating margin 39.4%.
- AI contribution: AWS AI business exceeded a $25B annual revenue run rate, growing at triple-digit YoY rate (~$6.25B quarterly run rate, roughly 15% of the $169B annualized revenue). Amazon did not disclose AI's precise percentage-point contribution to the 36.7% growth rate.

Microsoft Azure (Q3 FY2026, quarter ended March 31 2026):
- Cloud-services revenue grew 40% YoY (39% constant currency).
- AI services contributed ~12 percentage points of Azure's 40% growth (~30% of the growth rate).
- Total AI business reached a $37B annual revenue run rate, up 123% YoY.

Benchmark: Azure's 40% growth with AI contributing ~30% of that growth outpaces AWS's 36.7% growth, where AI's percentage-point contribution is not disclosed but the AI run rate ($25B) is smaller than Azure's ($37B). Both clouds report triple-digit AI revenue growth, but Azure quantifies AI's share of growth while Amazon does not.

Sources: S1.1/S1.2 (Amazon Q2 2026 earnings release), S2.1/S2.2/S2.3 (Microsoft Q3 FY2026 earnings), S8.1/S8.2/S8.3 (AWS AI disclosure commentary)."}
